title: Composition isomorphism of pullbacks of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, let $f\colon X\to Y$ and $g\colon Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes, and put $h=g\circ f$. Use the pullbacks of module objects of [def-sfb-module-upper-star] and the adjunctions $a_f:f^*\dashv f_*$, $a_g:g^*\dashv g_*$ and $a_h:h^*\dashv h_*$ of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Let $a_{g,f}:f^*\circ g^*\dashv g_*\circ f_*$ be the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and let $c:g_*\circ f_*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_*$ be the composition isomorphism of [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]. The composition isomorphism of pullbacks of module objects is the unique natural isomorphism
$$
b:h^*\xrightarrow{\sim} f^*\circ g^*\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_Z}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}
$$
whose conjugate under $a_{g,f}$ and $a_h$ is $c$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Equivalently, $b^{-1}:f^*\circ g^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*$ is the conjugate of $c^{-1}:h_*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_*\circ f_*$ under $a_h$ and $a_{g,f}$.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: (CategoryTheory.Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso a_g a_f a_h c).symm. Take C₀ = Mod_{Λ_Z}, C₁ = Mod_{Λ_Y}, C₂ = Mod_{Λ_X}, F₀₁ = g^*, F₁₂ = f^*, F₀₂ = h^*, G₁₀ = g_*, G₂₁ = f_*, G₂₀ = h_*. Functor composition in Lean is diagrammatic, so c has precisely the required type G₂₁ ⋙ G₁₀ ≅ G₂₀. The definition at CompositionIso.lean:72-74 is (conjugateIsoEquiv a_h (a_g.comp a_f)).symm c.symm, of type f^* ∘ g^* ≅ h^*. Taking its inverse gives b. The mate equation for b is exactly CategoryTheory.Adjunction.conjugateEquiv_leftAdjointCompIso_inv at CompositionIso.lean:82-86, with adjunction order (a_g.comp a_f), a_h. Uniqueness and the inverse equation follow from the bijections CategoryTheory.conjugateEquiv at Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean:275 and conjugateIsoEquiv at :425-435. CategoryTheory.Adjunction.comp at Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Basic.lean:567 constructs a_{g,f}. All categories, functors and adjunctions are arbitrary parameters, with no added geometric or coefficient hypothesis.
